ask.text: Tumne ghar mein kaunsi cheez kilograms mein dekhi hai?

body.teacherOpening: Namaste Riya! Aaj hum grams aur kilograms padhenge. Tumne ghar mein kaunsi cheez kilograms mein dekhi hai?

move.shape: greet Riya by name, warm and unhurried; one line on today's topic (Grams and kilograms); then one easy question about them; address them with tum forms (tum, tumhara, tumne), never tu

transcription.prompt: A young child aged 6 to 9 in India answers a teacher aloud in Hindi, English, or a Hindi-English mix. Write Hindi words in Devanagari and English words in Latin script, exactly as spoken.

move.shape: they asked to see it: a picture of the same idea; one idea; let the picture do the work; a few words about what to look at; the key stays unsaid; then one small question about what they see; address them with tum forms (tum, tumhara, tumne), never tu; the board draws what they asked for beside your words: say in plain words what it shows (its parts, its numbers); never send their eyes to the screen or the board, never say it is already there, never that you cannot draw, never ask them to draw it
move.must: never say there is no picture, never draw with characters; if the screen has it, first send their eyes there (dekho / look) and say what to see; if not, paint it in words

body.teacherReply: Dekho: ek tarazu mein 1 kilogram ka packet, doosre mein 1000 gram ke chhote packets—dono barabar. Tum kya dekh rahi ho?
